guidance.heading: Outlook and capital allocation strategy
section: Our focus on customer outcomes generates strong levels of growth, sustainable profits and significant cash flow. This financial strength enables us to maintain robust cash balances and the flexibility required to execute our long-term mission while returning excess capital to our owners.

● | In July 2026 we commenced a new share repurchase program, expected to be over $500 million, of which c.40% is expected to be allocated to our recurring EST share purchase program. To date we have purchased almost 50% of the expected total amount
The operating leverage in our business model and our ability to balance growth investment with profitability are also reflected in our forward-looking expectations. As of November 12, 2026:
● | Wise expects FY27 net revenue growth to be in the upper half (17.5-20%) of our 15-20% medium-term target range on a constant currency basis1*
● | Wise expects FY27 income before tax (‘IBT’) margin** around the top of our 20-25% range

* Net revenue on a constant currency basis is translated using the average monthly exchange rates from the comparable prior period for operations with functional currencies other than the U.S. dollar. We present net revenue on a constant currency basis, which is a non-GAAP financial measure, to facilitate comparison of underlying growth trends without the effects of exchange rate fluctuations. Please see below for reconciliation from the closest GAAP financial metric:

** Income before income taxes margin, which is a non-GAAP financial measure, is calculated as income before tax divided by net revenue, each as presented in our condensed consolidated statement of comprehensive income.

1 Guidance for net revenue growth includes recent increases to interest rates made by central banks, assumes no material change in the proportion of interest paid to customers and omits any further income or expense that may result from further changes in central bank rates that may occur.

desk.headline: Net revenue up 23% to $1.45bn, profit before tax up 9%; FY27 growth still seen in upper half of 15–20% range, margin near top of 20–25%
results: Net revenue rose 23% to $1.45bn (22% at constant currency); cross-border volume grew 24% to $141bn, led by the US and Asia Pacific.
Card revenue jumped 43% to $252m and cross-border revenue rose 19% to $705m, even after a 2 bp cut in the average fee to 0.50%.
Interest income on customer balances rose 16% to $464m; balances grew 22% but yields were lower.
Costs rose 28%, including about $15m of one-off listing costs, so profit before tax grew a slower 9% to $335m (23% margin).
A share buyback of over $500m started in July and is almost half done.

guidance.summary: Wise expects FY27 net revenue growth in the upper half (17.5–20%) of its 15–20% medium-term range at constant currency, and a pre-tax margin around the top of its 20–25% range. This matches what it said with its Q2 update on 16 Oct.

points: Management presented the lower take rate as a deliberate investment in cheaper prices to win customers.
Growth in investment and operating costs is expected to slow in the second half, excluding one-offs.
Guidance assumes no big central bank rate moves; the Bank of England's recent 25bp hike is not built in.
The Belgian prosecutor matter was settled with no admission of wrongdoing; the CFO said the cost is not material and terms stay private.
Wise Platform (bank partners) grew nearly 50%, with two large North American banks added.

watch: Whether cost growth slows in H2 as promised, lifting the margin toward 25%.
Interest income if central banks cut or raise rates, and further take-rate cuts.
Pace of new bank partners on Wise Platform and US product launches.
